messages:
Arjun Desai: quick data point from the quant cost experiments this week — SCM estimate vs measured looks good for most model families, but we’ve got a pretty big mismatch on **Qwen2-72B**.

Arjun Desai: tl;dr: SCM predicts Q4_K_M should be ~22–25% cheaper vs fp16 baseline (compute+mem). Measured $/1k tok improvement is only ~6–9% on our A100-80G pool, and basically flat on H100 in eu-west.

Arjun Desai: notebook + raw logs: https://drive.google.com/.../quantization-cost-experiments-log (see “2025-02-11_qwen2-72b_*” tabs)

Dr. Maya Srinivasan: :eyes: what’s the workload shape? prefill-heavy or decode-heavy? and are we comparing same latency SLO or just raw throughput?

Arjun Desai: both. we ran:
- short chat: 512 in / 128 out
- long gen: 2048 in / 512 out
- embeddings-ish: 128 in / 0 out (prefill only)

Arjun Desai: for fairness we held p95 latency target constant (same routing policy), then looked at tokens/sec + GPU-min attribution from telemetry.

Hassan Mirza: when you say “measured cost”, is that telemetry metered attribution (gpu_time_ms * sku_rate) or wall-clock from the harness?

Arjun Desai: telemetry-based. using the metered attribution prototype from Nadia’s pipeline (gpu_active_ms + allocator bytes) + SKU table. harness wall clock is consistent with telemetry (directionally), but I didn’t want to mix.

Nadia Rahman: yep, the experiment job is pulling from the same metering series we’re wiring into SCM. should be apples-to-apples except for the assumptions SCM is making.

Jordan Lee: do we know which assumption is driving that 22–25%? i.e. is it mostly compute scaling (ops/token) or memory bandwidth / kv cache?

Arjun Desai: mostly compute. our quant profile metadata right now says:
- q4_k_m: compute_multiplier = 0.78
- kv_cache_multiplier = 1.00
- activation_mem_multiplier = 0.85

Arjun Desai: SCM applies compute_multiplier uniformly to prefill+decode compute components.

Mateo Alvarez: that uniform compute multiplier is likely wrong for Qwen2-72B (or at least for our kernels). we’re not hitting GEMM-bound decode as much as on llama3.

Mateo Alvarez: for Qwen2 we’re spending more time in attention kernels + memory movement. quant reduces matmul cost but the runtime ends up memory/latency limited.

Sofia Ivanova: +1. batching also changes it. if the experiment fixed p95 latency, scheduler may be running smaller effective batches on Qwen2 because of the different token timing distribution. then you lose the batching efficiency gains that SCM assumes.

Arjun Desai: we did capture batch_size_effective. that’s another weird part: Qwen2 q4 shows batch_size_effective ~1.2–1.4 lower than fp16 for the same test. didn’t expect that.

Logan Wright: could be metric tagging gap? we had a couple of places where quant_profile_id was missing on decode spans, and then we backfilled from request-level tags. if the join is off, you can get mismatched batching series.

Arjun Desai: good call. for these jobs I see quant_profile_id present at request-level, but I didn’t verify it’s on both prefill+decode child spans.

Nadia Rahman: i can spot-check one run. paste a request_id?

Arjun Desai: e.g. `rq_01HTYQW2ZJ9K0...` (from “2025-02-11_qwen2_longgen_a100”)

Nadia Rahman: looking. decode spans have quant_profile_id, but prefill spans are missing it in ~30% of traces. backfill is happening, but it’s backfilling to “unknown” sometimes when the request context is dropped (we saw that in staging).

Jordan Lee: that can definitely skew if SCM is pulling prefill/decode split + quant from different dimensionality.

Mateo Alvarez: but even with clean tags, i buy the underlying perf story. Qwen2 attention path is different and the quant kernels aren’t giving us the same win.

Dr. Maya Srinivasan: we need to separate “instrumentation bug” vs “model-family exception.” both are actionable but different.

Laura Bennett: from unit economics POV: this is exactly the kind of thing that’ll bite Optimize recommendations. if SCM says “swap to q4 save 25%” and customer sees 5%, we need either lower confidence or a family-specific factor.

Hassan Mirza: Optimize side: we can gate recs on SCM confidence, but SCM needs to surface that confidence appropriately. right now quant profiles are treated like deterministic multipliers.

Jordan Lee: proposal:
1) short-term: for Qwen2-72B, add a per-model override (or “model_family_adjustment”) in the quant profile metadata used by SCM.
2) medium-term: compute_multiplier should be (prefill, decode) split, not a single scalar.
3) confidence: if telemetry indicates “memory-bound” (e.g. dram_bw near cap / low SM occupancy), downgrade expected savings.

Sofia Ivanova: +1 on prefill vs decode multipliers. also if batch_size_effective drops, SCM should not assume constant batch efficiency when comparing profiles.

Logan Wright: on telemetry: we can add an “effective_batch_efficiency_ratio” already computed in runtime metrics (post-admission). for Qwen2 it might be materially different with q4.

Mateo Alvarez: also check whether Qwen2-72B q4 is forcing a different kernel path (no flash-attn variant). that would explain smaller gains and batch behavior changes.

Arjun Desai: i can run a microbench w/ kernel selection logs enabled. will take a day.

Dr. Maya Srinivasan: action items:
- Arjun: rerun 2 cases with kernel debug + ensure quant_profile_id tags are present on both prefill+decode spans (coordinate w/ Nadia/Logan).
- Nadia/Logan: file bug for prefill span context drop + backfill-to-unknown issue (this is likely impacting SCM explain outputs too).
- Jordan: draft SCM adjustment plan: either per-model overrides or split multipliers. align with “deterministic + explainable” constraint.
- Laura/Hassan: note for Optimize: temporarily suppress “quant swap saves X%” for Qwen2 family until SCM v1.1 has the fix, or at least label as low confidence.

Hassan Mirza: ack. i’ll put a guard in the sweep: if model_family in {qwen2} then require confidence >= 0.8 else no recommendation.

Laura Bennett: pls also add a short note we can reuse for support: “quant savings are model+workload dependent; estimates may vary; see explain output.” we’ve got a few customers asking already.

Arjun Desai: :thumbsup: will update the quant-profile-cost-attribution-guidelines draft with “Qwen2 exception / attention-bound” section once we confirm.

Mateo Alvarez: ping me when you have kernel logs; i can help interpret. if we’re falling off flash-attn, we may be able to fix runtime too (not just SCM).

Dr. Maya Srinivasan: thanks all. let’s keep this thread updated w/ rerun results + whether mismatch persists after the tagging fix.
